case.trigger_text: Automated risk model alert: online purchase of $980.00 on Product R from an unrecognized Android device with anonymous.com email, 4.4x above cardholder median.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay switched off new_device_burst and device_churn (C4_new_device.md) as well as per-card micro-charge voting (LR 0.63). With only 2 small prior charges (avoiding the R5 3-charge card testing threshold) and no ring/cohort links, Assay treats this exact ATO pattern like HHF-009—closing or only verifying instead of blocking—and even if it flags e3, its capped episode builder misses e1 and e2, keeping exposure under $1,000 to evade FILE_REPORT.

idea: Bypass the uncapped episode builder (N7) and R7 recurring-charge rule during a session-hijack ATO by disguising four fraudulent drains over 9 days as the cardholder's normal home-device activity, then triggering a customer dispute on one charge that mimics a recurring monthly bill.

case.trigger_text: Customer called to dispute online charge of $79.99 ( matches monthly recurring billing amount on file); cardholder states their account credentials were compromised last week and they did not authorize this week's activity.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Because the attacker hijacked the customer's home session (device='home', p_email='home', addr1='home', low risk_score), e1-e3 look completely benign and spaced 3 days apart. Assay's capped dispute episode builder (N7) will either fail to aggregate e1-e3 into the fraud episode—severely under-counting the $1,445.49 exposure and skipping FILE_REPORT under R2—or misclassify the dispute under R7 (Disputed but legitimate) because the trigger mentions a monthly recurring amount.

idea: Evade TigerGraph ring detection (`ring_wcc`), `recipient_fanin`, and `micro_drip_cohort` across 5 compromised accounts by using 16 cards on a shared desktop profile to trip the >15-card ring cap, while keeping ATO cash-outs to 5 cards and $85+ amounts.

case.trigger_text: Model alert on Product H online transfer of $220.00 to recipient domain yahoo.com.mx using cardholder's usual email and billing address.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay drops shared device elements appearing on >15 cards (Ring caps: 16 cards use the Windows 10 profile), so `ring_wcc` ignores the shared device. Meanwhile, the 5 compromised accounts (C1-C5) sending ~$200 to `yahoo.com.mx` stay below the ~10-12 card minimum for `recipient_fanin` and way above the micro-amount threshold for `micro_drip_cohort`. Assay misses both the fraud verdict and the R6/§3a requirement to link and report connected cards.

idea: Trigger a false-positive escalation or block on a legitimate customer who looks like an ATO/dormant-wakeup victim by combining a dormant card wake-up (LR 5.65) with a misleading 'online' keyword in the alert text for an in-person transaction (exploiting the R8 record-conflict guard).

case.trigger_text: Velocity & Dormancy Alert: Card inactive for 35+ days woke up with $65.00 followed by $540.00 after customer updated online banking profile preferences.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: The cardholder is legitimately using their previously dormant card in person in their home billing region after logging into online banking. However, Assay's `dormant` detector fires with LR 5.65, its January drift guard prevents the moderate 0.29 risk score from clearing the case, and the word 'online' in `trigger_text` versus `channel='in_person'` trips Assay's naive R8 record-conflict guard (like HHF-008), tricking Assay into judging a legitimate customer as `uncertain` or `fraud` instead of `legitimate`.
